keyFindings.description: setEnvoyRole's refusal branch is the fourth site of the fence convention, and it was not fixed with the other three. `const waitingOnReap = await observeAbandonedHold(topic, role, result.holder)` (:1947) is an await, and `if (!waitingOnReap) refusedRoles.set(id, role)` (:1948) writes shared state after it with no live() re-read; observeAbandonedHold itself writes abandonedHolds.delete(topic) (:1859) and abandonedHolds.set(topic, ...) (:1862) after its own await of client.getRole, and takes no Fence at all. reassertRoleNow is the fenced sibling doing the identical endRole()/refusedRoles.set pair behind `if (!live() || claimedRoleTopic !== topic || !sessionOpen(id)) return false` at :1671-1674. Sequence (defaults: heartbeatMs 90000, passDeadlineMs 90000, a failing listener call costing the full 10250 ms budget): a degraded listener makes a move's hand-backs fail into abandonedHolds, the move burns ~82 s, setRole answers claimed:false, observeAbandonedHold makes a real getRole call, the 90 s deadline fires while it is in flight, the next move (or envoy_role_set, or the Legion bridge's claim at :2419) claims the role and does refusedRoles.delete(id) at :1915, and then the abandoned move's getRole answers and refusedRoles.set(id, role) at :1948 lands over it. desiredRole's want() at :2004 then answers undefined for that session, the next pass sees held !== desired and calls handBackRole() (:2295-2296), endRole() closes every whileHolding notice subscription and client.unsubscribe releases the role at the listener. Nothing re-claims it: refusedRoles is cleared only by a successful claim (:1915) or a session event (:2559). For a controller pane the daemon then reads no live holder (packages/daemon/internal/controller/liveness.go:125-127) and takes the role from a pane that is still running - the failure this issue exists to stop. It also falsifies the PR body's claim that an abandoned task writes nothing when it wakes. Fix: thread the Fence into observeAbandonedHold and re-read it before both abandonedHolds writes, and re-read live() between :1947 and :1948, mirroring :1671. Do it by naming one predicate per scope rather than adding a fourth hand-written guard.

registeredAt is process-global ('this process last had a registration accepted'), not per session, so the backstop's age test at :1751 measures from the old session's acceptance after a switch. Sequence: a pass is wedged (healing true); the backstop posts at tick T and sets registeredAt = T; the user runs /new, rebind sets sessionID synchronously (:2560) and queues a reconcile that cannot run behind the wedged pass; every tick until T+90 s then returns at :1751, so the new session is absent from GET /v1/sessions for up to one refresh interval while its pane runs. Strictly better than before this change, but it is a residual case of the symptom the backstop is advertised to close, and the comment at :1745-1746 ('a session that never had one accepted counts as older') is true only for the first session of a process. Fix: key registeredAt by the session the registration was accepted for and compare against the live sessionID at :1751, or reset it when the id moves.

startNotice takes an env parameter whose only use is to re-derive the resolver's own decision from the raw environment: `Number(env.ENVOY_PASS_DEADLINE_MS)` and `named > 0 && named < envoy.heartbeatMs` are a hand-copy of the usability test at envoy-settings.ts:257-260 plus the floor at :278, one module away from where that decision is made. Every other adjusted-setting line in this function reads a resolved, typed field (envoy.inbound.off at :101). The two copies can desynchronise on any future change to parsing. Fix: have envoySettings report the adjustment it made as a resolved field and let startNotice print it; the predicate then exists once and startNotice keeps its four parameters. NOT part of this finding, and not re-raised: that the MIN_INTERVAL_MS floor and MAX_INTERVAL_MS cap are applied in silence. The architect declined that this round and the PR body records the decline.

Two assertions can never fail: they assert that the check's output does not contain 'Equality is the rule met exactly' and 'do not .fix. it by widening', strings that exist nowhere in the tree - they were removed from the check by 783b97bd11b3 in this same pull request (grep over the workspace finds them only in these two assertions). They are vacuous forever and tell a future reader that some live path might still emit them. Delete both. The sibling at :131-132 earns its keep only while the fixture at :54 writes a MIN_PASS_DEADLINE_MS line into every generated tree, which is worth one comment.

The header says 'Three things must hold, and this check fails unless all three do:' and then lists four numbered rules (:14, :22, :30, :37); round 3 added rule 4, the pluginHeartbeat equality, without moving the sentence. This header is what a developer reads when the gate trips. One word. Related, and worth either a rule or a line of header: notice_exceptions.go:37-38 keeps listenerSessionTTL and listenerClaimStale as hand-copies of registry.go:116 and claim.go:14, and rule 1's own remedy text tells a maintainer to raise the registry ttl - the change that desynchronises them. The check already loads both files.

roundOneFindingsVerified: envoy.ts:2243 reads live() at the top of each hand-back iteration and breaks before the delete; the failed-hand-back restore runs past the fence deliberately and cannot overwrite a newer move's entry.

envoy.ts:1904-1913 records an accepted-but-abandoned claim as a pending hand-back before throwing, and settleEndedHolds settles it on the next pass; the unit case now asserts the hand-back instead of the leak.
envoy-settings.ts:276-280 floors the resolved passDeadlineMs at heartbeatMs, so no configured value can put the backstop out of reach; session-settings.ts says at start when a deadline was raised.

DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_MS is 90_000 and the check's rule 1 is three intervals plus one listener call's budget (280250 ms against 300000 ms), with the daemon's window at 4 x Heartbeat = 360000 ms, which covers the lifetime and still holds a pane on the old 120 s interval.

pluginHeartbeat is 90 * time.Second, the two 'every 2 minutes' sentences in claim.go and delivery.go are gone, the daemon test derives its schedule from noticeReholdDelays, and the constant is rule 4 of the check.
ensureConnection(live) dials into a local and re-reads the fence, shuttingDown and a connection another pass established in one synchronous block, closing the loser.
The check's worst case is 2 * heartbeat + call_budget, attributed to the backstop in the header and the failure text, and says the pass deadline is not read there.
The smoke reads both numbers from the two files that define them at run time (smoke-registration-stall.sh:70,75).
